plan: Given the common knowledge of rationality, the optimal bidding strategy converges to bid half of your value. This is because any bid higher than half your value risks winning the auction and paying too much, while any bid lower risks losing the auction when winning would have been profitable. My value is $24, so half is $12. I will bid $12.

Given the common knowledge of rationality and a single round, the optimal bidding strategy converges to bidding your true value. This is because any bid below your value risks losing the auction to a slightly higher bid, resulting in a loss when you would have profited. Any bid above your value risks overpaying. Since this is round 1 with no history, I will bid my true value of $16.

Given the common knowledge of rationality, the optimal bidding strategy converges towards bidding your true value minus a small increment. This is because any bid above your value risks winning the auction at a loss. Bidding too low risks losing the auction to someone bidding closer to their value. Since this is round 1 and we have no history, I will bid slightly below my value to attempt a win at a reasonable price.
